subject: Offline image trustflow & update orchestration — NovaHealth private deployment
messages:
From: Liam Burns <liam.burns@edgecloud.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Offline artifact signing / update channel for NovaHealth private deploy

Hi Aisha —

Hope you’re well. NovaHealth’s infra/security team is preparing an air-gapped private deployment for a portion of their PHI workloads. They asked me to confirm Redwood’s recommended pattern for:

- offline artifact distribution (USB vs. dedicated transfer station),
- image signing / attestation (we already use an HSM), and
- approved update orchestration (how to push patches without internet).

Specifically they want to know:
1) Do you provide a prescriptive manifest format we can use for offline updates?
2) How do you recommend protecting signing keys and supporting revocation in an offline context?
3) What does verification look like on the node (installer checks, SBOM / signature validation)?

Can you loop in your engineering folks for a technical review? They are targeting a POC in early November and need a short checklist + any scripts/tools you recommend.

Thanks,
Liam
EdgeCloud — Partner Integrations
[Attachment: prelim-network-map.png (image)]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Liam Burns <liam.burns@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Offline artifact signing / update channel for NovaHealth private deploy

Liam — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. I’ve put together a short plan and attached a YAML manifest template + a supply-chain checklist to get NovaHealth started. High level:

- Manifest + Attestation: We recommend a small TUF-like manifest (we call it the offline-trust manifest) that lists bundle hashes, versioning, and a signing chain. We’ve attached redwood-offline-signing.yml as an example.

- Signing + Key custody: Use your HSM to sign the top-level manifest. For customers that are fully air-gapped we support two patterns:
  * Customer-managed HSM: keys never leave the customer HSM; signing happens on-prem via an operator-run signing step (we provide signing helpers).
  * Hosted signing ceremony: for customers who permit an occasional escorted transfer, we can provide a signing appliance image plus a one-time export of a verification key.

- Transfer and chain-of-custody: Recommend a dedicated transfer workstation (locked, auditable) rather than ad-hoc USB swaps. The transfer tool — redwood-offline-sync — is a small CLI that:
  1) validates signed manifest signatures,
  2) verifies per-file SHA256 checksums,
  3) writes the bundle to the installer staging area with an attestation record.

- Node verification and rollback: The installer verifies the manifest signature and per-artifact signatures (cosign attestation + SBOM verification). We support atomic swapping of container/rootfs with a verified rollback pointer and a signed rollback manifest so nodes can safely revert.

Next steps I propose: quick technical call with Vivek + Jonas to validate the manifest and installer hooks, and Neha to confirm key-ceremony checklist and KMS/HSM integration steps. I’ve attached the YAML + checklist.

Would a 45-minute slot on Thursday (10/14) work? If yes I’ll schedule and send an agenda.

Attachments: redwood-offline-signing.yml (template), supply-chain-checklist.xlsx (checklist)

—
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0192

From: Liam Burns <liam.burns@edgecloud.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-10-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Offline artifact signing / update channel for NovaHealth private deploy

Thanks Aisha — that looks promising. A few follow-ups from NovaHealth security:

- Transfer media: they’ll insist on write-once media where possible. Is your redwood-offline-sync able to produce signed transfer artifacts with a chained checksum (so the transfer station can later prove the file set came from the manifest)?
- Kernel / boot-level verification: they currently require signed kernels and UEFI Secure Boot. Can the installer verify kernel signatures and fail-safe if chain-of-trust is broken?
- Key rotation & revocation: in an air-gap scenario how do you recommend handling key compromise? Are there procedures to publish a revocation manifest that nodes will honor on next offline check?

Also — can you share a short example of the on-node verification log output so their auditors can see what evidence will be produced during an update?

Liam
Liam Burns
EdgeCloud — Systems Integration

Subject: Fwd: Offline artifact signing / update channel for NovaHealth private deploy — action items

Forwarding the thread with NovaHealth / EdgeCloud. They want a concise POC plan and auditor-facing evidence for an air-gapped private deployment. Below are the action items we agreed on during the sync:

> (quoted) From: Liam Burns <liam.burns@edgecloud.io>
> To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
> Date: 2026-10-13T11:05:00-07:00
> Subject: Re: Offline artifact signing / update channel for NovaHealth private deploy
>
> Thanks Aisha — that looks promising. A few follow-ups from NovaHealth security: ...

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Vivek: Produce a short architecture doc (2-3 pages) for redwood-offline-sync showing how manifest signing, cosign attestations, and on-node verification interact. Include a sample on-node verification log snippet. Due: 2026-10-20.
- Neha: Draft a key-ceremony checklist (HSM-first pattern) and a revocation workflow (signed revocation manifest flow + emergency key rotation instructions). Include recommended audit log fields. Due: 2026-10-19.
- Jonas: Validate the installer’s kernel/UEFI verification steps and confirm rollback semantics; provide a short test plan for the POC. Due: 2026-10-21.
- Aisha: Own the POC timeline, coordinate procurement for a transfer workstation, and send the external DocuSign link for the PO. Due: 2026-10-18.

Meeting: I’ve proposed the 45-minute technical call on 2026-10-14; if that slips we’ll rebook. POC window requested by NovaHealth: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-12.

I’ve attached the starter signing template and a signed sample bundle for reference (installer-bundle-v1.2.tar.gz.sig). Please upload drafts to the shared Drive folder and ping me when each item is ready so I can send to the customer and their auditors.

Thanks team — this POC is important for the NovaHealth renewal conversation, want to make the technical evidence airtight.

—
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
